title: Natural cancellation of scalar extension in sheaf tensors
statement: Let (C,J) be a site, let R and S be sheaves of commutative rings, and let α : R → S. Write U for restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] and E(N) for the sheafified sectionwise extension of scalars [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For every S-module sheaf M and R-module sheaf N there is an R-module isomorphism U(M ⊗_S E(N)) ≅ U(M) ⊗_R N, natural in both M and N. No flatness assumption is required.

source.place: Tag 05V4, lemma-flat-change-of-rings, displayed tensor identity; Section 03EK, sheaf tensor construction

proof.text: On sections over W, use the balanced R(W)-linear equivalence m ⊗ (s ⊗ n) ↦ (s m) ⊗ n with inverse m ⊗ n ↦ m ⊗ (1 ⊗ n). The inner R-balancing follows from the restricted action on M, and the outer S-balancing follows from associativity of that action. Tensor induction gives both inverse identities. The formulas commute with restrictions, since α is natural and restrictions on M are semilinear. They commute with module maps f and g because f(s m) = s f(m), giving a presheaf tensor isomorphism natural in both factors.

Restriction of scalars commutes with module sheafification. Extend the restricted S-sheafification unit using the R-module sheafification adjunction. On underlying abelian sheaves the resulting map is the identity of the same abelian sheafification, so it is invertible because forgetting module structure reflects isomorphisms. The same underlying identity proves naturality in every presheaf map.

Let η be the sheafification unit of the sectionwise scalar extension E_p(N). Monoidal localization says that sheafification inverts M.val tensor η. Consequently S-sheafification of M.val tensor E_p(N) is naturally isomorphic to M tensor E(N). Restrict this isomorphism, apply the comparison of step 2, sheafify the isomorphism of step 1 over R, and apply the inverse sheaf-tensor comparison over R. This gives the claimed isomorphism. Naturality of the sheafification unit, of its counit, and of the monoidal tensorator, together with step 1, proves its naturality in both factors. The formulas also apply to zero rings and modules.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_changeOfRings_tensorCancellation (α : R ⟶ S) :
    ∃ e : ∀ (M : SheafOfModules.{max u v} (𝓡 S))
        (N : SheafOfModules.{max u v} (𝓡 R)),
      (restrictScalars (𝓻 α)).obj
        ((monoidalCategory S).tensorObj M (changeOfRings α N)) ≅
      (monoidalCategory R).tensorObj ((restrictScalars (𝓻 α)).obj M) N,
      ∀ {M M' : SheafOfModules.{max u v} (𝓡 S)}
        {N N' : SheafOfModules.{max u v} (𝓡 R)} (f : M ⟶ M') (g : N ⟶ N'),
        (restrictScalars (𝓻 α)).map
            ((monoidalCategory S).tensorHom f (changeOfRingsHom α N g)) ≫
          (e M' N').hom =
        (e M N).hom ≫
          (monoidalCategory R).tensorHom ((restrictScalars (𝓻 α)).map f) g
